N00c-pwa-lock-llm-proxy.guard_resolution: RESOLVED. The client passes the producer's own objects through instead of flattening to data-URL strings, so WeakSet identity survives the signature change. assertApprovedAttachments() fails closed: unmarked, unknown-type, hand-built or non-object all throw. A byte-level second witness exists only so a framework-cloned block is not FALSELY blocked; it can admit nothing that was not itself redaction output.

N20x-ocr-contrast-regression.root_cause: Photographed monitors glue W onto PLUS. ContrastStatus.detect() requires a standalone ' W ' token; with the W glued only ' WO ' survives, so a with-and-without study resolved as WITHOUT — 70553 (2.23) became 70551 (1.45), a 0.78 wRVU under-count per affected study. Confirmed by dumping real pipeline output for um-worklist-2837: only row 10 ('MRI BRAIN WPLUS WO CONTRAST') was affected; every correctly-spaced row already resolved.
N20x-ocr-contrast-regression.fix: Isolate PLUS during contrast normalisation so the token boundary is restored whichever side was glued. Modelled against a 12-case battery first: corrects all three glued variants, zero regressions on the nine correct cases.

N25x-examdate-precision.finding: CloudSyncService.swift:177 sends examDate at full ISO8601 second precision. Under Safe Harbor any date finer than the year is an identifier, so the cloud store is a limited data set rather than de-identified data. Truncating to DAY in the sync payload (keeping second precision on device) is a small change with real compliance value and should not wait for Phase C.

N25y-redact-names.finding: Redaction.redact() covers labelled MRN/DOB/SSN, SSN-shaped, date-shaped and 5+ digit runs — roughly 4 of the Safe Harbor 18. NAMES are not redacted at all, and a name is the identifier a worklist actually contains. Mitigated but not solved by the escalation path's fragment caps, consent sheet and the edge API's own dob|mrn|ssn rejection.
